If the pricing scan of $L$ from residual weights $r$ and total price $P$ ends with residual weights $r'$ and total price $P'$, then…
nodes.title: Pricing scan: the total price is at most what a cover pays

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be rational residual weights with $r(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, let $P$ be a rational number and let $L$ be a list of edges (ordered pairs of vertices). If the pricing scan of $L$ from residual weights $r$ and total price $P$ ends with residual weights $r'$, then every pair $(u, v)$ in $L$ has $r'(u) = 0$ or $r'(v) = 0$.
nodes.title: Pricing scan: every edge has an exhausted endpoint

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be rational residual weights with $r(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, let $P$ be a rational number and let $L$ be a list of edges. If the pricing scan of $L$ from residual weights $r$ and total price $P$ ends with residual weights $r'$, then $0 \le r'(v) \le r(v)$ for every vertex $v$.
nodes.title: Pricing scan: residual weights stay between $0$ and their start

nodes.summary: Given rational residual weights $r$ on the vertices, a rational total price $P$ and a list of edges (ordered pairs of vertices), the pricing scan processes the edges in order: an edge $(u, v)$ has price $\delta = \min(r(u), r(v))$, which is subtracted from the residual weight of $u$ and of $v$ (once if $u = v$) and added to the total price. The result is the final pair of residual weights and total price, and the…
nodes.title: Pricing scan

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be rational weights on a finite vertex set with $w(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, and let $L$ be a list of edges (ordered pairs of vertices). For every pair $(u, v)$ in $L$, $u$ or $v$ belongs to the set returned by the pricing method on $w$ and $L$.
nodes.title: The pricing method covers every listed edge

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set, let $w$ be rational vertex weights with $w(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, and let $L$ be a list of ordered pairs of vertices such that for every edge $uv$ of $G$, the pair $(u, v)$ or the pair $(v, u)$ is in $L$. Then the set returned by the pricing method on $w$ and $L$ is a vertex cover of $G$.
nodes.title: The pricing method returns a vertex cover

nodes.summary: For all rational vertex weights $w$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and every list $L$ of edges, the pricing method on $w$ and $L$ takes exactly $|L| + |V|$ time units, where $|L|$ is the length of the list: one unit per listed edge and one per vertex.
nodes.title: Running time of the pricing method

nodes.summary: Let $w$ be rational weights on a finite vertex set with $w(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, let $L$ be a list of edges (ordered pairs of vertices), and let $C$ be a set of vertices such that every pair $(u, v)$ in $L$ has $u \in C$ or $v \in C$. Then the total weight of the set returned by the pricing method on $w$ and $L$ is at most $2 \sum_{v \in C} w(v)$.
nodes.title: The pricing method weighs at most twice any cover of the listed edges

nodes.summary: Given rational weights $w$ on a finite vertex set $V$ and a list of edges (ordered pairs of vertices), run the pricing scan on the list starting from residual weights $w$ and total price $0$, then return the set of vertices whose final residual weight is $0$. On top of the cost of the scan, the selection costs $|V|$ time units.
nodes.title: Pricing method for weighted vertex cover

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite vertex set, let $r$ be rational residual weights with $r(v) \ge 0$ for every vertex $v$, let $P$ be a rational number and let $L$ be a list of edges. If the pricing scan of $L$ from residual weights $r$ and total price $P$ ends with residual weights $r'$ and total price $P'$, then $\sum_{v \in V} (r(v) - r'(v)) \le 2 (P' - P)$.
nodes.title: Pricing scan: the vertices pay at most twice the price
